title: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era
content_md: Written by: George Manuelian, Chief Strategy Officer, RapidFort The modern software stack has become an iceberg. The application code customers and security teams see at the surface is only a small portion of what is being shipped. Beneath it sit operating systems, frameworks, libraries, packages, and transitive dependencies, with much of it drawn from open source or third parties. As AI accelerates software development, that hidden complexity has become an even more critical security challenge. For business and technology leaders, the question is no longer simply how many vulnerabilities exist. It is where does meaningful risk live, which vulnerabilities can be exploited in our environment, and how we can reduce that risk without turning developers into full-time vulnerability managers. The answer requires a fundamental shift from vulnerability accumulation to continuous software resilience. The typical containerized stack is layers of base operating system software, packages, libraries, language frameworks and dependencies, and the application itself. The application a company writes may represent only a small portion of what it ultimately ships. That is important because vulnerabilities multiply. A vulnerable package in a base image is not necessarily one vulnerability in practice; it can be replicated across every application and container that uses that image.
